analysis: The changed file is a Swift test file (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift). The patch adds a decodeTable to the test stub tokenizer (head lines ~146-155), threads a stopStringScope parameter through the test helper makeBridge (head ~443, ~462), and adds a test for EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence scoped stop reporting (head 847-899). The supplied units are base text (lines 1264-2457) and contain none of the changed ranges, which sit earlier in the file. I reviewed the base text of the shared-budget, cancellation, capacity, factory and lookup-receipt tests for security-relevant behavior. These exercise the TB-007 KV budget gating, reservation release on teardown and rejection, and SSD prefix-cache staging and reservation release (T-041). All of this is test-only code with no production behavior change, no new attack surface, no secrets, and no changes to authorization, attestation, encryption or key custody. The tests do reinforce the T-041 mitigations: reservations are released on every path, cache scope is passed through, and SSD staging is abandoned on cold fallback. Remaining questions concern the production-side change to EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence and the stop-string scope (CBv2StopStringScope). Those source files are not in this batch, so a separate pass should check that scoped stop handling does not alter output integrity or leak reasoning content.
